chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Joseph Reinhardt's playing
summary: Briggs says Django's brother Joseph played decent solos in clubs but was inspired by and subordinate to Django.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: So that let me just recapitulate that, just to make sure that we got this correct.
So, this would have been around in 1933, maybe.
Yes, it was about '33, getting around '34.
I see, and you had this band at this club which you had an investment in the club?
And Django was in the band, and these other fellows were in the band, and they would just take kind of a
little special set that they'd play in that group.
The question that I have, did you ever hear Joseph Reinhardt play a solo?
Yes, I heard him play a solo. He played now and then, not bad.
But he wasn't as good as Django?
No, no. Not as good, because he was inspired by his brother.
'Cause he -- I don't think he ever soloed on any record.
No, he never soloed, 'cause probably his brother didn't allow him to solo. But in playing in a cabaret or playing in a place, he soloed --
